newsitem.title: UK: BT - no comment on ITN windfall tax story.
newsitem.headline: BT - no comment on ITN windfall tax story.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc, the UK's largest telecoms operator, refused to comment on a television report on Wednesday which claimed the company would be liable for the new Labour government's windfall tax on privatised utility profits.

The Independent Television News(ITN)report quoted unnamed Whitehall(government)sources but did not give any further detail. The BT spokesman told Reuters that she could not comment on the ITN story until the company had seen a transcript of the report.
"The devil is often in the detail," she said.
"We will await details of the windfall tax in the budget."

BT said it did not expect to be caught in the windfall-tax web, details of which are expected to be announced during Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's first budget address to parliament on July 2.
"We are not a monopoly -- we have around 200 licensed competitors and operate in an open market. We have paid tax since privatisation in 1984 and we continue to invest in the UK and cut prices."
She reiterated the group's stated position it would "consider a legal challenge" if cited under the windfall tax provision, but said such a move would depend on whether BT was "stung in a big way."
